text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers.

- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said today the Employees' Provident Fund must first prove its capability in building low and medium-cost houses before volunteering to shoulder additional tasks like establishing a housing development board.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said today Malaysia is disappointed with the unilateral decision by the United States to attack Iraq and may ask the Organisation of Islamic Conference to adopt a common stand on the matter.

- Malaysia's national van and truck manufacturer Industri Otomotif Komersial (M) Sdn Bhd aims to dominate the light commercial vehicle market within five years with its models based on the Renault Trafic van and Hyundai Porter truck.
- Effective checks against overloaded lorries have started with the Public Works Department's handing over all but one of 43 weighbridges to the Road Transport Department.
- Plans to establish a national housing board that might have direct links with the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) are on the drawing board.

- The Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Ministry is looking into the concerns expressed by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) over the recent amendments of two sections of the Companies Act 1965. The amendments require companies' numbers to be inscribed on their common seal and on all documents.
